gap: No result ChatGPT got states that ChatGPT's own 'best overall value' pick, the Anker 351 (A9192, $28.99 on anker.com), lists no clamping voltage and no UL certification on its maker page (only TUV, CP65, FCC and ICES), while Belkin's 12-outlet SRA009P12TT8 costs $29.99 on belkin.com and lists 400 V line-to-neutral clamping, a $300,000 connected-equipment warranty and UL 1449 certification.
standout_why: I fully read only HonestFred (result 2 in chat 1, result 4 in chat 2). It names Wirecutter's Tripp Lite TLP1208SAT and Tom's Guide's Anker 351, but says its author did not test the products and did not verify prices. It also gives no clamping voltage, no warranty and no prices. Fetching failed for the two cited rivals: Tom's Guide returned only its title, Good Housekeeping blocked the fetch, and the Yahoo copy of the Good Housekeeping list returned 403. So I can't rule out that they print clamping voltages. ChatGPT's own answer says to look for UL 1449 but then makes the Anker its top pick, and the Anker page doesn't show UL. That suggests the cited pages didn't make this point clear.
decides: The pick may change. ChatGPT's #1 'best overall value' (Anker 351, $28.99) doesn't meet the UL 1449 test ChatGPT itself sets, going by Anker's own page. For $1 more, the Belkin SRA009P12TT8 ($29.99 at belkin.com, which beats the $39.09 Staples price ChatGPT showed) publishes 400 V clamping, a $300,000 warranty and 3,780 J. Catch: belkin.com shows it out of stock ('Coming Soon'). Belkin's PivotPlug BP112230-08 is $49.99, $5 above the $44.99 ChatGPT showed, and also out of stock until 2026-11-19. Our TESSAN PS07 is $28.99, the same price as the Anker, with 2,100 J, 8 outlets and 20 W USB-C. Where it loses: its maker text, read through the store search, shows no clamping voltage or UL listing, and it has 8 outlets to the Anker's and Belkin's 12.
